# Areté — academic companion for the University of Uyo

> ἀρετή (ar-eh-TAY). A free study companion for University of Uyo undergraduates in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria: the outline, recommended textbooks and study tips for all 95 courses from 100 Level to Final Year, transcribed lecture notes and past-paper practice for a growing set of them, interactive Java, Python and C tracks, a capture-the-flag security track, and an AI tutor that has read the curriculum.

- Site: https://www.aretecyb.tech
- Institution: University of Uyo (https://www.uniuyo.edu.ng/, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q7896523)
- Audience: 100 Level – 400 Level undergraduates
- Scope: the whole university, not one department. 29 of the 95 courses below are foundation courses taken across University of Uyo programmes rather than owned by any one department (a programme takes either GST 211/311 or GST 212/312, for instance, but every programme takes some of these): GST 111, MTH 111, PHY 111, PHY 117, COS 111, STA 111, UUY-CSC 111, UUY-CSC 112, GST 121, COS 121, MTH 121, PHY 121, PHY 128, GST 212, COS 211, ENT 221, COS 221, INS 224, GST 312, CSC 319, COS 411, ENT 321, GST 211, MTH 211, MTH 212, MTH 223, CSC 223, GST 311, INS 411. They are marked "foundation course" in the listing.
- Departments with a fully authored catalogue: Cybersecurity, Data Science. A student in any other department signs up in foundation mode and gets those shared courses plus all four programming tracks; more catalogues are authored as students from those departments sign up.
- Access: course outlines, textbooks and study tips are public. Lecture notes, question banks, the AI tutor and progress tracking need a free account (email code, no password).
- Last generated: 2026-09-09

## Courses

- [All 95 course outlines](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses): the hub, grouped by year.

### 100 Level

- [COS 111 — Introduction to Computing Sciences](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cos-111): 3 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. A broad survey of the computing field: hardware, software, human-ware, information processing, and the many specializations within computing. Lays the conceptual vocabulary and hands-on device familiarity for everything that follows in your degree.
- [GST 111 — Communication in English](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/gst-111): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Develops the English language skills required for academic and professional success: sound patterns, word classes, sentence construction, logical/critical reasoning, and writing craft. A foundation course that improves every other course you will take.
- [MTH 111 — Elementary Mathematics I (Algebra and Trigonometry)](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/mth-111): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Algebra and trigonometry for university-level computation: set theory, real and complex numbers, sequences and series, quadratic equations, and circular measure. Bridges secondary-school maths with the rigour needed for the programme.
- [PHY 111 — General Physics I (Mechanics)](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/phy-111): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Classical mechanics: vectors, kinematics, Newtonian dynamics, conservation principles, rotational motion, and gravitation. Builds the physical intuition that underpins electronics, networking signals, and the hardware concepts met in later computing courses.
- [PHY 117 — General Practical Physics I](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/phy-117): 1 unit, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Laboratory practicals that accompany PHY 111. Quantitative measurement, treatment of measurement errors, and graphical analysis across mechanical, electrical, light, heat, and viscosity experiments. Develops precision, scientific method, and report-writing discipline.
- [STA 111 — Descriptive Statistics](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/sta-111): 3 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. The language of data: types, sources, and methods of data collection; presentation, errors and approximations; and the core measures used to summarise a dataset. A foundation for every analysis task in research and data-driven decision-making.
- [UUY-CSC 111 — Computer Operations](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-csc-111): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Practical computer skills: laboratory safety, hardware components, operating system navigation, productivity software, internet operations, and an introduction to statistical computing with SPSS. The hands-on companion to COS 111.
- [UUY-CSC 112 — Computer Troubleshooting](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-csc-112): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Diagnosing and resolving common hardware and software problems across PCs, laptops, tablets, and mobile phones. Covers network connectivity/security troubleshooting, backup and restore, and virus/anti-virus procedures — practical skills every computing professional needs.
- [UUY-DTS 111 — Fundamentals of Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-111): 3 units, First Semester. Your orientation to the discipline: what data science actually is, what a data scientist does day to day, and the end-to-end lifecycle of a data project from question to deployed insight. Heavily practical — you will handle real datasets in your first semester.
- [UUY-DTS 112 — Introduction to Database Technology](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-112): 2 units, First Semester. How data is stored, structured and retrieved at scale. Relational modelling, normalisation, and SQL — the single most reusable practical skill in the degree, and the one most often tested in data-science job interviews.
- [COS 121 — Problem Solving](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cos-121): 3 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Algorithmic thinking and systematic problem solving using Python and C. Covers problem identification, solution techniques, pseudocode/flowcharts, and programming fundamentals — the first real programming course in the degree. Strong performance here builds confidence for all future programming courses.
- [GST 121 — Nigerian Peoples and Culture](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/gst-121): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. An introduction to Nigeria's ethnic diversity, cultural heritage, colonial and political history, and nation-building challenges. Provides context for the social and policy dimensions of technology in Nigeria.
- [MTH 121 — General Mathematics II (Calculus)](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/mth-121): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Single-variable calculus: limits, continuity, differentiation, integration, and their applications. Builds the analytical foundation for probability, statistics, and the signal theory used across science and engineering.
- [PHY 121 — General Physics II (Electricity & Magnetism)](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/phy-121): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Electrostatics, DC circuits, magnetism, and electromagnetic induction. The electromagnetic foundations of this course directly underpin networking, wireless communications, and electronics studied in later years.
- [PHY 128 — General Practical Physics II](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/phy-128): 1 unit, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Laboratory practicals continuing from PHY 117, covering the theoretical concepts of PHY 121 through quantitative measurement, treatment of measurement errors, and graphical analysis.
- [UUY-CYB 121 — Introduction to Computer Networks](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-121): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundational networking: how data travels across local and wide area networks, the OSI/TCP-IP models, IP addressing and subnetting, routing protocols, and simulation with Packet Tracer. Critical groundwork for network security courses in later years.
- [UUY-CYB 122 — Principles and Practice of Information Security](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-122): 2 units, Second Semester. An introduction to the core principles of information security: operating system protection mechanisms, intrusion detection, formal security models, cryptography and steganography, and the policy/regulatory dimension of protecting information and value across networks.
- [UUY-CYB 123 — Web Authoring and Development](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-123): 2 units, Second Semester. Building web pages from scratch: web architecture and the client-server model, HTML structure, CSS styling, JavaScript interactivity, and XML documents. An entry point into web security topics and the front-end layer targeted by many cybersecurity attacks.
- [UUY-DTS 121 — Foundation of Web Technologies for Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-121): 3 units, Second Semester. How the web works and how to get data out of it. HTML, CSS and JavaScript fundamentals, HTTP and APIs, and the beginnings of web scraping — because a great deal of the data you will ever analyse lives behind a URL.
- [UUY-DTS 122 — Introduction to Information and Communication Management](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-122): 3 units, Second Semester. How organisations create, move, store and govern information, and how ICT infrastructure supports that. The organisational context in which data work actually happens — systems, stakeholders, policy and communication.

### 200 Level

- [COS 211 — Computer Programming I](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cos-211): 3 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Object-oriented programming in Java: from variables and control flow through full OOP, collections, exception handling, file I/O, and GUI development with Swing. The primary programming course of the degree and the subject most likely to determine your programming competence throughout your career.
- [CYB 211 — Introduction to Cybersecurity and Strategy](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-211): 2 units, First Semester. A strategic overview of the cybersecurity landscape: basic concepts (confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, non-repudiation), security policy and incident response, risk management, and the national/organisational strategies that guide security decision-making at scale.
- [CYB 213 — Cybercrime, Law and Countermeasures](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-213): 2 units, First Semester. The legal and regulatory landscape of cybercrime: Nigerian cybercrime law, international frameworks, types of cybercrime, investigative procedures, and technical countermeasures. Essential context for any cybersecurity professional.
- [DTS 211 — Introduction to R Programming](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-211): 2 units, First Semester. R from the ground up: the language, its data structures, and the tidyverse workflow for importing, tidying, transforming, visualising and modelling data. R is the statistician's language, and it is the fastest route from a dataset to a publication-quality figure.
- [DTS 212 — Introduction to Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-212): 2 units, First Semester. The formal treatment of the data science process, building on UUY-DTS 111: problem formulation, data acquisition, feature construction, model families, evaluation, and the ethics and limits of inference from data.
- [GST 211 — Philosophy, Logic and Human Existence](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/gst-211): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Philosophical method, formal logic, and the perennial questions about knowledge, value and human existence. The logic half is directly technical — it is the same propositional calculus you will formalise in MTH 212 and implement in code.
- [GST 212 — Philosophy, Logic and Human Existence](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/gst-212): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. An examination of philosophical reasoning, formal logic, and the human condition. The logic component — syllogism, symbolic logic, and rules of inference — directly supports discrete mathematics and the formal reasoning used in security proofs and algorithm design.
- [MTH 211 — Mathematical Methods I](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/mth-211): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. The analytical toolkit for scientific computing: sequences and series, partial differentiation, vector calculus and an introduction to differential equations. These are the methods that underpin optimisation, gradient-based learning and statistical modelling.
- [MTH 212 — Sets, Logic and Algebra](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/mth-212): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Rigorous foundations: set theory, formal logic, relations and functions, and an introduction to abstract algebraic structures. This is where mathematical proof is taught properly, and where the language of the rest of your theoretical courses is set.
- [SEN 211 — Introduction to Software Engineering](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/sen-211): 2 units, First Semester. The principles and practices of building software systematically: software development lifecycle models, requirements engineering, system design, testing, and project management. Context for how secure software is planned and built.
- [UUY-CYB 212 — Ethical Hacking Fundamentals](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-212): 2 units, First Semester. An introduction to offensive security thinking: information security fundamentals, the hacking cycle, and countermeasures across passwords, social engineering, networks, web/mobile/IoT applications, wireless, and the cloud. Covers the legal/ethical framework under which penetration testing operates.
- [UUY-CYB 214 — Fundamentals of IoT](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-214): 2 units, First Semester. The architecture, protocols, market segments, and security challenges of the Internet of Things. Covers sensing/actuation, cloud data collection and analysis, smart-city and industrial use cases, and the unique vulnerabilities of IoT devices — a rapidly growing attack surface.
- [UUY-DTS 211 — Introduction to Data Analytics](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-211): 2 units, First Semester. Analytics as a business discipline: the four analytics types (descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive), KPI design, dashboarding, and turning an analysis into a decision. Practical and tool-focused.
- [COS 221 — Computer Programming II](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cos-221): 3 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Advanced programming building on COS 211: deeper object-oriented programming (polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces), the Collections API, searching/sorting/recursion, event-driven and GUI programming. Bridges programming skills and the algorithmic thinking required for security tool development.
- [CSC 223 — Discrete Structures](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/csc-223): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. The mathematics of discrete objects — counting, graphs, trees, recurrence relations and Boolean algebra. Graph theory in particular is the direct foundation for network analysis, recommendation systems and the web-data work in UUY-DTS 311.
- [CYB 222 — Cybersecurity Innovation and New Technologies](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-222): 2 units, Second Semester. Emerging technologies and their cybersecurity implications: AI in security, blockchain, quantum computing threats to cryptography, zero-trust architecture, and the innovation lifecycle in the security industry.
- [CYB 224 — Information and Big Data Security](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-224): 2 units, Second Semester. Big data fundamentals — characteristics, sources, platforms, and analytics — paired with the security side: information and big data security requirements, lifecycle security management, risk management, and cloud-based big data security.
- [DTS 224 — Statistical Inference and Modelling](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-224): 3 units, Second Semester. Reasoning from a sample to a population: estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and the linear model. The core statistical machinery of the degree — and the part most often misused in practice.
- [DTS 226 — Probability for Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-226): 3 units, Second Semester. The mathematics of uncertainty: probability axioms, random variables, distributions, expectation, and the limit theorems. Probability is the language machine learning is written in — every model output is ultimately a probability statement.
- [ENT 221 — Entrepreneurship and Innovation](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/ent-221): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Business thinking for technical students: entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship theory, entrepreneurial characteristics and thinking, innovation, enterprise formation, and e-commerce principles. Directly applicable to consulting, startup, and freelance careers in technology.
- [INS 224 — Systems Analysis and Design](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/ins-224): 3 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. A structured approach to analysing information system needs and designing solutions: the software development lifecycle, top-down and bottom-up design, dataflow diagramming, entity-relationship modelling, and file/database and user-interface design.
- [MTH 223 — Introduction to Numerical Analysis](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/mth-223): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. How to compute answers to mathematical problems that have no closed-form solution, and how to know when the computed answer is wrong. Error, convergence and stability — the reason floating-point arithmetic sometimes betrays you.
- [UUY-CYB 221 — Network Defense Fundamentals](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-221): 2 units, Second Semester. Practical network security: identification/authentication/authorization, threat classification, firewalls, administrative/physical/technical controls, virtualization and cloud, wireless/mobile/IoT security, and cryptography/PKI. Builds directly on the networking foundation from UUY-CYB 121.
- [UUY-CYB 222 — Web and Mobile Applications Security](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-222): 2 units, Second Semester. Attacking and defending web and mobile applications. Covers the OWASP Top 10 in depth, secure coding practices for Java/Python/Kotlin/Swift, audit and QA testing, and mobile-specific threats on iOS and Android platforms.
- [UUY-DTS 224 — Programming in Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-224): 2 units, Second Semester. The working Python data stack: NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and scikit-learn. Where the mathematics of the other 200 Level courses becomes code you can run on a real dataset.

### 300 Level

- [CSC 319 — Artificial Intelligence](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/csc-319): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Foundations of AI: intelligent agents, search algorithms, knowledge representation, semantic networks, natural language processing, and expert systems. Directly relevant to AI-powered anomaly detection, prediction, and automated analysis across computing.
- [CYB 311 — Cryptography Techniques, Algorithms and Applications](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-311): 2 units, First Semester. The mathematical and algorithmic foundations of modern cryptography: symmetric and asymmetric cryptosystems, key management, hash functions, digital signatures, PKI, and protocol security. The theoretical backbone of all secure communications.
- [CYB 312 — Biometrics Security](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-312): 2 units, First Semester. Biometric authentication systems: digital image/signal processing, matching algorithms, error metrics, and data security. Covers implementation in national identity systems and access control.
- [CYB 313 — Cybersecurity Risks Analysis, Challenges and Mitigation](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-313): 2 units, First Semester. Systematic methods for identifying, analysing, and treating cybersecurity risks. Covers applied information security management, risk mitigation in the cloud, governance and security policy, the ISO 27000 series, and the economic/geopolitical factors behind Africa's cyber risk exposure.
- [DTS 312 — Big Data Computing](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-312): 2 units, First Semester. What changes when the data no longer fits on one machine. Distributed storage and computation, the MapReduce model, Hadoop and Spark, and the architectural patterns of modern data platforms.
- [DTS 314 — Data Management I](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-314): 3 units, First Semester. Database systems for the data professional, going well beyond UUY-DTS 112: advanced SQL, indexing and query performance, transactions and concurrency, and the design of data models that survive real workloads.
- [DTS 318 — Ethics and Legal Issues in Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-318): 2 units, First Semester. The obligations that come with holding and modelling data about people: privacy law, consent, algorithmic fairness, transparency and accountability. The course that determines whether your technical skill does good or harm.
- [GST 311 — Peace and Conflict Resolution](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/gst-311): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. The nature of conflict, the conditions for peace, and the practical machinery of resolution — negotiation, mediation and arbitration. Applied to the Nigerian and West African context.
- [GST 312 — Peace and Conflict Resolution](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/gst-312): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. The causes, dynamics, and resolution of conflict in a multi-ethnic nation: types and theories of conflict, root causes of conflict and violence in Africa, peacebuilding strategies, and the roles of international organisations, media, and traditional institutions.
- [UUY-CYB 314 — Information Security Models](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-314): 2 units, First Semester. The formal models that underpin access control and multi-level security: Bell-LaPadula, Biba, Clark-Wilson, Brewer-Nash, and the access-control mechanisms (MAC, RBAC, ACLs, lattice-based control) that implement them in real systems.
- [UUY-CYB 315 — Lab for Cyber Attacks and Vulnerability Testing](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-315): 2 units, First Semester. Hands-on laboratory course in offensive/defensive security: operating system file structures, formal security models, intrusion detection, vulnerability testing, and countermeasures for denial-of-service, worm, and virus attacks.
- [UUY-CYB 316 — Database Management and Control Systems](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-316): 2 units, First Semester. Securing database systems from the ground up: installing and configuring a database product, security architecture and operating-system security principles, user/privilege/role administration, and database auditing models and practice.
- [UUY-DTS 311 — Analytics of Web Data](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-311): 2 units, First Semester. Measuring and analysing behaviour on the web: clickstream and log data, web analytics platforms, funnels and attribution, plus text and network analysis of web content. Builds directly on UUY-DTS 121.
- [UUY-DTS 313 — Machine Learning and Applications](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-313): 2 units, First Semester. The core machine learning course: supervised and unsupervised algorithms, how they are trained, how they are evaluated, and how they fail. The technical centrepiece of the degree.
- [UUY-DTS 317 — Basic Operating Systems for Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-317): 2 units, First Semester. Operating system fundamentals with a practical Linux emphasis: processes, memory, file systems, the shell, and containers. The environment every data pipeline actually runs in.
- [CYB 311 — SIWES I (Student Industrial Work Experience Scheme)](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-311-siwes-1): 3 units, Second Semester. The first industrial training placement: three months attached to a private or public organisation during the second-year long break, gaining practical cybersecurity experience under supervision, with a defended report at the end.
- [CYB 312 — SIWES II (Student Industrial Work Experience Scheme)](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-312-siwes-2): 3 units, Second Semester. The second, more advanced industrial placement: three months attached to a private or public organisation during the third-year long break, building on SIWES I with additional practical cybersecurity experience and a defended report.
- [CYB 313 — Report Writing](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-313-report-writing): 3 units, Second Semester. The craft of professional and technical report writing, focused on documenting the SIWES I and II placements: structuring findings, presenting technical work clearly, and defending a written report before a panel.
- [CYB 314 — Mini Project](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/mini-project-300l): 3 units, Second Semester. A supervised mini research or development project that demonstrates integration of skills acquired across the first six semesters. Serves as a preparation and rehearsal for the 400L Final Year Project.
- [CYB 399 — Seminar](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/seminar-300l): 3 units, Second Semester. A series of student-led presentations on advanced topics in cybersecurity. Develops research, critical analysis, and public speaking skills in a professional academic setting.
- [DTS 399 — SIWES](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-399): 6 units, Second Semester. Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme — a full-semester supervised industrial placement. Six units and 270 practical hours, the largest single course in the programme, assessed on your logbook, technical report and defence.
- [UUY-DTS 321 — Computing Skills](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-321): 3 units, Second Semester. A wholly practical course consolidating the professional toolchain: version control, environments, testing, documentation and deployment. The skills that make you employable rather than merely knowledgeable.
- [UUY-DTS 322 — Industry-based Innovation](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-322): 3 units, Second Semester. A practical, industry-facing innovation project: identify a real problem in an organisation or sector, design a data-driven solution, and demonstrate it. Runs alongside SIWES and feeds directly into your final-year work.
- [UUY-DTS 323 — Seminar](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-323): 3 units, Second Semester. Research and presentation skills: select a current topic in data science, review the literature, and present and defend it before staff and peers. Preparation for the literature review and defence of DTS 417/428.

### 400 Level

- [COS 411 — Research Methodology and Technical Report Writing](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cos-411): 3 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. The rigorous methods for conducting and communicating academic and technical research: research types and approaches, scientific investigation and problem formulation, data collection instruments, and the structure of technical reports. Essential preparation for the Final Year Project.
- [CYB 411 — Systems Vulnerability Assessment and Testing](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-411): 2 units, First Semester. Advanced vulnerability assessment methodology: systematic identification, testing, and mitigation of risks to a company's infrastructure. Covers penetration testing methodologies, information gathering, password cracking, social engineering, and reporting at a professional level.
- [CYB 412 — Steganography: Access Methods and Data Hiding](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-412): 2 units, First Semester. The art and science of concealing information: history of secret writing, steganography vs encryption, text/image/audio/video steganography techniques, information hiding and steganalysis, and steganography detection.
- [CYB 413 — Cyber Threat Intelligence and Cyber Conflict](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-413): 2 units, First Semester. Techniques for detecting, responding to, and defeating organised cybercrime and cyberwar activities. Covers cyber threat intelligence (tactical, operational, and strategic), the kill chain, indicator lifecycle, and the evolution of counterterrorism and cyber conflict.
- [CYB 414 — Cloud Computing Security](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-414): 2 units, First Semester. Securing cloud environments: cloud service and deployment models, data-centre and virtualisation security, the cloud cube model, threat mitigation, and the standards (NIST, Cloud Security Alliance) that govern effective cloud management.
- [CYB 497 — Final Year Project I](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-497): 3 units, First Semester. The first phase of the capstone Final Year Project: an independent or group investigation of a cybersecurity-related problem, culminating in a written proposal covering the problem statement, objectives, scope, research gap, and proposed methodology. Supervised closely by an academic supervisor.
- [DTS 413 — Data Visualization for Data-driven Decision Making](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-413): 2 units, First Semester. The theory and craft of visual communication: perception, encoding, chart selection, dashboard design and narrative. How an analysis becomes a decision.
- [DTS 417 — Final Year Project I](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-417): 3 units, First Semester. The first half of the capstone: choose a problem, review the literature, design the methodology, secure the data, and defend a proposal. What you do this semester determines whether DTS 428 is manageable or miserable.
- [INS 411 — Project Management](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/ins-411): 2 units, First Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. Planning, executing and controlling projects: scope, schedule, cost, risk and stakeholders, across both traditional and agile approaches. Directly applicable to running your final-year project on time.
- [UUY-CYB 411 — Business Intelligence in Small and Medium-Scale Enterprises (BISME)](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-411): 2 units, First Semester. Data analytics and business intelligence tools in the context of small and medium enterprises: BI applications in Excel and R, reporting tools, data warehousing and dimensional modelling, ETL, and how BI connects to big data and cloud computing.
- [UUY-DTS 410 — Special Topics in Data Science](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-410): 2 units, First Semester. A rotating course on current developments in the field — the content varies year to year with staff expertise and what is moving in the discipline. Recent themes include deep learning, large language models, MLOps and causal inference.
- [UUY-DTS 411 — Bio-Analytics Systems and Applications](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-411): 2 units, First Semester. Data science applied to biological and health data: genomics, clinical records, epidemiological modelling and public-health surveillance, with the specific statistical and ethical challenges those domains bring.
- [UUY-DTS 412 — Data Management II](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-412): 2 units, First Semester. Enterprise-scale data management, continuing DTS 314: data architecture, pipelines and orchestration, master data and quality management, governance, and the modern data stack.
- [CYB 421 — Ethical Hacking and Reverse Engineering](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-421): 2 units, Second Semester. Advanced offensive security: perimeter defences, privilege escalation, malware and social engineering, system and network hacking, web/wireless/mobile attacks, and reverse engineering of code and network exploits as a method for developing countermeasures.
- [CYB 422 — Deep and Dark Web Security](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-422): 2 units, Second Semester. The architecture, technologies, and security landscape of the dark web. Covers Tor network internals, cryptocurrency and crypto-trading, safe and anonymous access techniques, and the risks and monitoring of dark/deep web activity.
- [CYB 423 — Digital Forensics and Investigation Methods](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-423): 2 units, Second Semester. The science and practice of digital forensics: securing, processing, acquiring, examining, and reporting digital evidence; the cyber trail; and the role of computers in crime, technology, and law. Covers portable and stationary device forensics.
- [CYB 498 — Final Year Project II](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/cyb-498): 3 units, Second Semester. A continuation of CYB 497: completing the research methodology, statistical data analysis, prototype/simulation development, and the formal written report (chapters four and five), submitted for final grading with an oral defence before the external examiner.
- [DTS 426 — Data Science Innovation and Entrepreneurship](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-426): 2 units, Second Semester. Entrepreneurship specific to data: what makes a data product commercially viable, how data businesses are structured, and how to price, protect and scale an offering built on data and models.
- [DTS 428 — Final Year Project II](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/dts-428): 3 units, Second Semester. The capstone completed: implement the methodology designed in DTS 417, evaluate the results, write the full report and defend it. The single largest determinant of your final-year classification.
- [ENT 321 — Venture Creation](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/ent-321): 2 units, Second Semester. Foundation course: taken across programmes. The practical mechanics of launching a business: opportunity identification, business planning, entrepreneurial finance, marketing and e-commerce, and applying emerging technologies to new ventures. Prepares graduates who want to start consultancies or technology ventures.
- [UNIUYO-CYB 425 — VoIP and Multimedia Security](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uniuyo-cyb-425-voip): 2 units, Second Semester. Securing voice-over-IP and multimedia traffic: VoIP network architecture and call-control protocols (H.323, SIP, MGCP), NAT/firewall traversal, and the encryption and best practices that mitigate VoIP-specific risks.
- [UUY-CYB 424 — Enterprise Security and Information Assurance](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-cyb-424): 2 units, Second Semester. Security governance at the enterprise level: information security principles, governance and risk management, security architecture and design, and end-to-end security of e-business and cyber environments — from data-centre security to backup and disaster recovery.
- [UUY-DTS 421 — Data Science Risk and Management](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-421): 2 units, Second Semester. What goes wrong with data and models, and how to manage it: model risk, data risk, operational failure, and the governance structures that catch problems before they reach production.
- [UUY-DTS 422 — Cloud Application Development](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-422): 2 units, Second Semester. Building and deploying applications on cloud infrastructure: service models, core compute and storage services, containers and serverless, and the deployment of data and ML workloads to the cloud.
- [UUY-DTS 423 — Data Warehousing and Multidimensional Modeling](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-423): 2 units, Second Semester. Designing the analytical database: dimensional modelling, star and snowflake schemas, slowly changing dimensions, OLAP operations, and the ETL that populates it all.
- [UUY-DTS 424 — Intelligent Computing and Analytics for Urban Centres](https://www.aretecyb.tech/courses/uuy-dts-424): 2 units, Second Semester. Data science applied to cities: sensor and IoT data, mobility and transport analytics, geospatial analysis, and the smart-city systems that use them — with the Nigerian urban context front and centre.

## Guides and tools

- [Install Java, Python and C](https://www.aretecyb.tech/install): JDK 17 + Apache NetBeans for the COS 211
  and COS 221 labs, Anaconda + JupyterLab for Python, GCC via MSYS2 for C.
- AI Tutor: answers scoped to a student's year, department and course outline (account only).
- Code Explainer: line-by-line plain-English walkthroughs of Java, Python, C and C++ listings.
- Study Planner: weekly timetables exported to .ics or synced to Google Calendar.
